direct_ffi_candidates.vsock_add_tap: regular exported vsock tap registration function
direct_ffi_candidates.vsock_remove_tap: regular exported vsock tap unregistration function

linux/netdevice.h.reason: Expose `net_device`, `net_device_ops`, `dev_lstats_read`, flags, and per-cpu stat enums needed by vsockmon planning.

linux/virtio_vsock.h.reason: Expose `VIRTIO_VSOCK_MAX_PKT_BUF_SIZE` for the current vsockmon MTU expression.

net/af_vsock.h.reason: The vsock tap and header layout should be hidden behind a dedicated Rust abstraction instead of leaking raw transport internals to driver code.

net/rtnetlink.h.reason: Expose `rtnl_link_ops`, `rtnl_link_register`, and `rtnl_link_unregister` for the link-type abstraction plan.

uapi/linux/vsockmon.h.reason: Expose the exported monitoring header type needed by the current MTU calculation.

vsock_tap.reason: vsockmon open/close lifecycle is defined around vsock tap registration rather than netlink tap registration.
required_surface: A private-state-owned vsock tap handle that stores `dev` and `module` before registration.
Open/stop helper methods that call `vsock_add_tap`/`vsock_remove_tap` in matched lifecycle points.

translation.goal: Constrain the first `drivers/net/vsockmon_rust.rs` to a profile-driven plan that exposes missing vsock-specific abstractions before driver codegen.
translation.abstraction_goal: Constrain Phase 4 so a future vsockmon Rust loop is blocked on explicit vsock tap and MTU abstraction work instead of ad-hoc driver invention.

mvp_scope.target_command: ip link add vsockmon0 type vsockmon && ip link set vsockmon0 up && ip link show vsockmon0 && ip link set vsockmon0 down && ip link del vsockmon0
mvp_scope.note: The first vsockmon loop should still target the same lifecycle oracle, but the profile must first expose vsock-specific tap and MTU abstractions.

body_plan: Only use the typed `netdevice::Device` setters listed in `setup_translation`.
Keep vsock-specific constants and header coupling behind abstractions rather than in driver code.
Access private state through the typed `private` argument only.
Access private state through the typed `private` argument only.
Receive the packet as owned `skbuff::SkBuff` and the device as shared `&netdevice::Device` only.
Return `netdevice::TxOutcome::Ok` without exposing helper FFI in the driver.

type.note: Keep device type selection inside the typed `netdevice::Device` wrapper.

priv_flags.note: Preserve the `IFF_NO_QUEUE` setup bit without raw field access.

lltx.note: Keep lockless TX configuration in the wrapper layer.

netdev_ops.note: Do not assign `dev->netdev_ops` in driver code; the rtnl abstraction wires it before `setup`.

ethtool_ops.note: Keep `ethtool_ops` out of the first Rust loop.

needs_free_netdev.note: Keep free-on-destroy policy inside the wrapper.

features.note: Keep the feature bit expression inside the typed netdevice abstraction surface.

flags.note: Preserve the `IFF_NOARP` setup bit through the typed wrapper.

mtu.note: The current MTU expression depends on vsock-specific exported constants and should be lifted behind a future dedicated abstraction.

pcpu_stat_type.note: Keep the setup write for parity, but do not enable `ndo_get_stats64` yet.

init_policy.rust_requirement: The private type must accept the all-zero bit pattern (`Zeroable`).

fields.name: tap
fields.note: Own the vsock tap in Rust private storage; the first loop should not expose raw transport tap state.
